notes: Sample config.json. Copy to config.json in the tool root and edit.

This file answers 'where does the tool put its own runtime state, and which declaration files does it read'. It deliberately holds no thresholds, targets or schedules - those are data/*.json, one file per decision.
Relative paths resolve against the directory holding this file, so a copied tool root stays self-consistent.

The tool root is found by a stated order and NOT by where the package sits on disk: DB_OPS_HOME, then the working directory when it holds data/ or config.json, then the package location. DB_OPS_DATA_DIR moves the data folder on its own. See docs/configuration.md.
'console_level' and 'file_level' are the two logging thresholds: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR.
'master' and 'worker' are only read by the control app (docs/11_control_app.md), which builds an image on one machine and deploys it to another. A single-machine install can delete both lists.
A worker node's 'password_ref' names a key in data/encrypted_secret_text.json - never a password itself.

master.description: Where the image is built and configuration is edited. The role of THIS process is declared at run time by DB_OPS_NODE_ROLE, so a config file copied between machines can never mislabel one.

worker.description: Linux host running the scheduled apps near the databases. 'user' and 'password_ref' let the control app authenticate with only the secret passphrase on the command line.
